title: Wari ceramic vessel, Museo Larco
summary: A painted vessel of the Wari culture, which ruled much of the Andes between about 600 and 1000 CE, now in the Museo Larco in Lima.

title: Chimú gold ornament, Museo Larco
summary: Gold work made in Chan Chan, capital of the Chimú kingdom on Peru’s north coast, between 1100 and 1400. Chimú goldsmiths hammered and joined thin sheets into large ornaments.

title: Moche seated-figure bottle
summary: A sculpted ceramic bottle from the Moche of Peru’s north coast. Moche potters modelled real people, animals and plants in clay.

title: Gold armlet, Museo del Oro
summary: A pre-Hispanic gold armlet in the Museo del Oro of Colombia’s central bank, which holds over 30,000 gold objects from the country’s Indigenous cultures.

title: Maya-Ulúa tripod vessel
summary: A painted tripod vessel from the Ulúa valley in western Honduras, made between 600 and 900, where Maya and neighbouring traditions met. Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino, Santiago.

title: Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino
summary: The Chilean Museum of Pre-Columbian Art in Santiago, which brings together art from Mexico to the far south of the Andes.

title: Museu Afro Brasil, São Paulo
summary: A museum in São Paulo’s Ibirapuera Park devoted to African and Afro-Brazilian art and history. Its collection includes material on the Malê, the enslaved African Muslims of Bahia.

title: Mezcala stone mask
summary: A carved stone mask of the Mezcala culture of Guerrero, in the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Mexico City.

title: Building a tadjah for Hosay, Cedros
summary: Craftsmen in Cedros, Trinidad, building a tadjah, the tall decorated model tomb carried in Hosay, the Muharram commemoration brought by Indian indentured labourers in the 1800s. Each tadjah takes weeks of bamboo, paper and tinsel work.

title: Hosay in Trinidad, 1910
summary: A 1910 photograph of Hosay in Trinidad, one of the oldest Muslim traditions in the Americas.

title: Museo Textil de Oaxaca
summary: The Textile Museum of Oaxaca, in an 18th-century house, shows the weaving and dyeing of Oaxaca’s Indigenous communities alongside textiles from around the world.

title: Huichol five-string guitar
summary: A Wixárika (Huichol) guitar with five strings, decorated in the bead and yarn work the Wixárika are known for. Museo de Arte Popular, Mexico City.

title: Maya water drum
summary: A water drum from the Yucatán Peninsula: a gourd floated in water and struck, its pitch changing with the water. Museo de Arte Popular, Mexico City.

title: Woven leather huaraches
summary: Hand-woven leather huarache sandals, a Mexican craft kept alive by family workshops. Museo de Arte Popular, Mexico City.
